verdict: The skipped signals were good trades, just slightly worse than the ones taken. Sde394f26 skipped 521 signals: they average +0.96R per trade against +1.25R for the 615 taken, with the same share of big (≥ 5R) winners. Sa016f4eb: +0.98R skipped vs +1.23R taken.

But you could not have traded them. 374 were skipped because all 10 slots were full and 135 for lack of cash. Even with no slot limit, cash still blocks 384 of them: each position is sized from a tight stop, so 10 positions already use most of the capital.
More slots add little and cost drawdown: 15–20 slots lift Sde394f26 from 13.7% to 14.2% but deepen the drawdown from −27% to −30%; Sa016f4eb goes from 14.8% / −21% to 15.0% / −24%. Keep 10.

The result is not luck in which signals were picked. Over 200 runs with random picks, Sde394f26's CAGR ranges 12.4–14.7% (5th–95th percentile, median 13.5%); the actual 13.7% sits in the middle. Sa016f4eb: 13.9–16.1%, median 15.0%, actual 14.8%.

Choosing the tightest stop first mainly helps the drawdown: the actual drawdown beats 86% (Sde394f26) and 74% (Sa016f4eb) of the random runs. Random picks give a median −29% and −23%, and up to −33% and −26%.

Practical reading: plan for 12–15% CAGR with drawdowns up to about −33% for Sde394f26, and 14–16% with up to about −26% for Sa016f4eb. Missing a signal in live trading is not a disaster; the edge is spread across all of them.

findings.title: Details
points: By period, skipped trades did better than taken ones in 2000–04 and 2010–14 and worse in 2005–09, 2015–19 and 2020–26. Ranking by tightest stop is not a strong selector of better trades; its value is smaller, safer positions.
Signals skipped during the drawdown pause were mostly losers for Sde394f26 (−0.34R on 12 signals), supporting the pause rule.
Signals skipped for lack of cash had the highest win rate (43–46%); they come late in strong markets when the book is full of winners.
No signal was skipped because the stock was already held: the monthly setup rarely fires twice while a position is open.

method.title: Method
points: The engine plays out every signal (entry, stop, exits) independently of the portfolio; the portfolio now logs each one as taken or skipped with the reason (results/studies/skipped/<D|C>/base/signals_none.csv).
R = (exit − entry) / (entry − stop): the trade's result in units of its initial risk, before costs.
Slot variants keep 1% risk per trade on current equity, the 20% position cap and the drawdown rule; only max_positions changes.
Random runs: same-day signals that compete for scarce slots are ordered randomly (seeds 0–199) instead of tightest stop first; everything else is unchanged.
